stories.title: MIT researchers say GPT-6 Astra can rewrite other models' weights directly
stories.summary: MIT researchers found OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can read and directly edit other models' weights without training, raising a Qwen model's math accuracy from 7.9% to 48.1% by changing just 0.016% of its weights.
stories.more: MIT researchers demonstrated that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can inspect and deliberately rewrite the weights of other AI models without using traditional training. In one experiment, Astra raised a Qwen model's math accuracy from 7.9 to 48.1 percent while altering only about 0.016 percent of its weights. The approach is described as a potential way to simplify AI optimization by editing weights directly rather than retraining. The researchers note the technique still hits clear limits, though the article does not specify what those limits are.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra sees the matrix and reprograms other AI models directly through their weights
items.excerpt: MIT researchers show that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can read and deliberately rewrite the weights of other AI models without traditional training. In one experiment, Astra boosted a Qwen model's math accuracy from 7.9 to 48.1 percent by changing just 0.016 percent of its weights. The approach could fundamentally simplify AI optimization but still hits clear limits. The article GPT-6 Astra sees the matrix and reprograms other AI models directly through their weights appeared first on The Decoder .

stories.title: Anthropic's FlashProve prototype verifies which model wrote a response
stories.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, a research prototype that uses cryptography to verify which AI model produced a given response without revealing the model's weights.
stories.more: Anthropic has released FlashProve, described as a research prototype rather than a finished product. The system uses cryptographic techniques to verify whether a given AI response actually came from the model it claims to, without exposing that model's underlying weights. The Decoder's report notes that the system still has significant limitations. No details on those limitations or on availability were included in the excerpt.

stories.title: Researchers propose LoCo to cut reasoning model inference costs
stories.summary: A new method called LoCo teaches large reasoning models to recognize when they already have enough information and stop deliberating, aiming to cut inference costs without hurting accuracy.
stories.more: Large reasoning models often keep generating chain-of-thought tokens even after they have gathered enough information to answer, driving up inference costs. Existing compression methods mostly trim finished reasoning trajectories rather than deciding in the moment whether more reasoning is actually needed. LoCo instead learns a local preference for stopping once the current reasoning state is sufficient, rather than operating after the fact on a full trajectory. The paper frames this as a preference-learning approach to reasoning compression. It does not specify in the available excerpt how much compute savings LoCo delivers or which models and benchmarks were tested.

items.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
items.excerpt: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. stories.title: Study factors MLLM embeddings to improve composed image retrieval
stories.summary: A new technique factors multimodal LLM embeddings to better capture requested image edits, aiming to improve composed image retrieval beyond relying on contrastive training alone.
stories.more: Composed image retrieval asks a system to find a target image given a reference image plus text describing a desired change. Recent methods use multimodal LLMs to generate a single retrieval embedding, but the researchers argue this underuses the model's compositional understanding because it maps queries straight into an embedding via contrastive supervision alone. Their method factors the embedding to more explicitly resolve the intended visual modification before retrieval. The excerpt does not specify which benchmarks were used or how much the factored approach improves accuracy over prior methods.

stories.title: Sam Altman defends RAM remarks, renames himself 'Ram Altman' on X
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman responded to criticism of his comments on PC RAM shortages by renaming his X account 'Ram Altman' and saying people should buy as much memory as they want.
stories.more: Sam Altman spent election night responding to backlash over earlier comments about PC RAM shortages. He changed his display name on X to 'Ram Altman' after a user's comment, saying he wants the world to have plenty of memory and for people to put as much RAM as they want into their computers. The exchange reflects ongoing public sensitivity around AI's role in memory chip demand and pricing. Further specifics of the original comments that triggered the backlash were not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company to expand Codex's coding tools
stories.summary: OpenAI announced it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, aiming to expand Codex's tools for building, understanding, and reviewing code.
stories.more: OpenAI said it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc., folding the startup's work into its Codex coding product line. The announcement frames the deal around expanding Codex's capabilities for building, understanding, and reviewing code, rather than naming a specific new feature. OpenAI did not disclose the acquisition price or Pierre's team size in the material available. It is also unclear when the acquired technology will ship inside Codex.

stories.title: Google's Search ad growth slows even as AI Overviews use climbs
stories.summary: Alphabet's Q3 earnings showed search query growth at a five-year high, but Search ad revenue growth slowed to 12 percent as AI features reshape how clicks turn into ad revenue.
stories.more: Alphabet reported that search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, according to its latest earnings report. Despite that growth, Google's Search revenue growth slowed to 12 percent year over year in the third quarter, down from about 17 percent the prior quarter. Growth in paid clicks, meaning clicks on ads, was also described as shifting, though the available excerpt cuts off before specifying the direction. The figures suggest Google has not yet found a way to make its AI-driven search features monetize as effectively as traditional search ads.

stories.title: Google faces backlash over plan to cut Search access for AI-restricting schools
stories.summary: Google drew criticism from politicians including NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani and former FTC chair Lina Khan over a reported plan to turn off Search for schools that restrict AI use.
stories.more: TechCrunch reports that Google is facing backlash over a plan that would disable Search access for schools that restrict AI tools. Politicians on the left, including New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani and former FTC chair Lina Khan, accused Google of acting like an unregulated monopoly. The criticism centers on Google allegedly using its market position in search to pressure schools' AI policies. Further details on the plan's scope or Google's response were not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: US midterm voters back curbs on data center expansion
stories.summary: Voters in Tuesday's US elections favored candidates and ballot measures that restrict data center construction, a setback for an AI industry that depends on rapid buildout.
stories.more: Data center developers are facing a more restrictive building environment after voters across the US elected candidates who favor moratoriums and backed ballot measures that add obstacles to expansion. The report cites an NBC News Election Day poll showing a notable share of voters expressing related concerns, though the exact figure was cut off in the available excerpt. The result is framed as a setback for a pillar of the AI industry's growth plans, which rely on continued data center buildout for compute capacity. It is unclear from the available details exactly which states' ballot measures or candidates were decisive.

stories.title: UK's £400 billion AI economic boost claim traced mainly to Google
stories.summary: The UK government's claim that AI would add £400 billion to the economy relied mainly on a Google-sourced estimate; the AI minister now says the real figure is under a third of that.
stories.more: Wired reports that the UK government's widely cited claim that AI would add £400 billion to the economy came mainly from a figure originating with Google. The country's AI minister has now conceded the actual estimate is less than a third of the original £400 billion figure. Researchers cited in the piece attribute part of the gap to the UK's slow rate of AI adoption. The article does not specify what revised figure the government is now using or when it was updated.

stories.title: Uber says AI agents booked just 4 rides and ~500 Eats orders in Q3
stories.summary: Uber executives said third-party AI agents arranged only four rides and about 500 Uber Eats orders in Q3 2026, suggesting agentic booking is still rare on its platform.
stories.more: During its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, Uber disclosed that third-party AI agents arranged just four rides in the quarter. The company said AI agents fulfilled a larger but still small number of Uber Eats orders, around 500. Uber executives used the figures to downplay concerns that AI agents booking services directly could disrupt its business soon. The numbers suggest consumer adoption of agentic shopping and travel booking remains limited for now, at least on Uber's platform.

stories.title: Op-ed warns enterprises need data lineage to secure AI agent handoffs
stories.summary: An MIT Technology Review piece argues that AI agents passing data to each other without human review creates security risk, and that enterprises need data lineage tracking to secure these workflows.
stories.more: The article describes a scenario where a sales AI agent pulls data from restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes to answer a query, and a second agent then uses that output to draft a proposal without human review. It argues this kind of unchecked agent-to-agent handoff creates security exposure for enterprises adopting agentic AI. The piece frames data lineage tracking as a way to secure these multi-agent workflows. Specific tools or vendors for implementing this lineage were not detailed in the available excerpt.

stories.more: Sulphur-3 is built on MiniMaxAI's MiniMax-H3 base model and is tagged on Hugging Face as a finetune of it. stories.title: HN discussion: AI is forcing companies to pay off decades of technical debt
stories.summary: A widely discussed Hacker News submission argues AI coding tools are pushing organizations to finally address 40 years of accumulated technical debt, drawing 569 points and 370 comments.
stories.more: The Hacker News submission links to an IEEE Spectrum article about AI in cybersecurity and a PHP-to-shell vulnerability, arguing that AI tools are pushing organizations to confront decades of accumulated technical debt. The discussion drew significant engagement, with 569 points and 370 comments on Hacker News. The original article's exact argument connecting AI adoption to technical debt and the cybersecurity vulnerability was not detailed beyond the title and URL in the available excerpt.
